02 / Hackathon project

AllAbout Campus

Students ask practical university questions. The tool visits relevant pages, answers with citations, and shows which sources it could and could not check.

Role
Team lead
When
September 2026
Tools
React, Fastify, Steel, Playwright
The project

Why we made it

Answers to course and campus questions are scattered across websites, calendars, and pages that may require a login. A plausible answer is not enough if a student cannot see where it came from or whether an important page was missed.

What I did

I led the team and joined the React interface, Fastify service, and live browser workflow. I worked on source routing, extracting evidence, and reporting coverage so the system could show inaccessible or insufficient sources instead of hiding them.

A useful resultAn answer with citations, plus a receipt of what was checked, skipped, or blocked by login.

How it works

The Course Desk accepts a question and shows a cited answer. The read-only browser panel lets a student see pages as they are reviewed. A coverage receipt distinguishes readable sources from pages that were skipped or required a login; local history lets a student reopen earlier questions.

Behind the interface, the server routes source visits through Steel and Playwright. Evidence extraction and shared contracts keep captured material connected to the answer. Live runs require configured API access. Labeled fixture runs are for repeatable demonstrations and are not represented as live research.

What we checked

Preflight and regression checks covered source routing, browser execution, cancellation, cleanup, and evidence integration. The result is a repeatable hackathon demo. It is not a complete university information service, and a cited answer can still miss a relevant rule.
